proof-narrative-lean-equiv.evidence: Lean proves `Summable` over ℝ for q > 1 only; the statement is over an abstract char-0 ring ("convergent" is undefined there) and its content, "represents the abstract grouplike", is not encoded. Proof: the recursion a_{m+1} = a_m/[m+1] ✓. False step: "[n]_q! → ∞ faster than geometrically when \|q\|< 1". For 0<q<1, [n]_q → 1/(1−q), so [n]_q! = (q;q)_n/(1−q)^n grows only geometrically and the radius of convergence is 1/(1−q). Counterexample q = 1/2: term ratio x/[n+1] → x/2, divergent for \|x\|> 2. The table's "0<q<1: … n! … radius ∞" is wrong for the same reason. The \|q\|= 1 "Diophantine" claim is unproved (\|[n]_q\|≤ 2/\|1−q\|bounds the radius)
